title: Vercel AI SDK Masterclass: From Fundamentals to Deep Research
talk_summary: A Vercel AI SDK tutorial covering generateText, tool calling with maxSteps, and generateObject, then building a recursive deep-research agent (breadth/depth search, relevance evaluation loop, accumulated state, final report).

takeaways.technique: Trim tool results to only relevant fields
takeaways.what_they_do: Before returning web results into model context, they map over results and keep only fields needed for the task, dropping favicons and other page chrome.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the language model is so much more effective when you trim away all of the irrelevant information

takeaways.technique: Local variables instead of model-parsed parameters
takeaways.what_they_do: For large payloads (crawled pages), they stash results in a closure variable and have the model only emit a small signal, rather than forcing the model to re-emit the whole payload as tool arguments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't want the model to have to actually parse that out. It's literally generating the text that already exists in the context above

takeaways.technique: Bounded agentic loop with explicit feedback on rejection
takeaways.what_they_do: A search/evaluate loop runs under maxSteps; when a result is judged irrelevant the tool returns a corrective instruction string that the next step sees.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Search results are irrelevant, please search again with a more specific query

takeaways.what_they_do: They pass previously used URLs into the evaluator and mark repeats irrelevant, so the same large page is never re-injected.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the page already exists in the existing results, mark it as irrelevant

takeaways.technique: System prompt with persona, date, and explicit output format
takeaways.what_they_do: Adding a system prompt (expert researcher, today's date, markdown, flag speculation) markedly improved report structure versus letting the model infer format.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in order to get the best response, you want to leave as little up to the model to infer as possible

takeaways.technique: Cheap model for steps, reasoning model for synthesis
takeaways.what_they_do: They use a single main model for search/eval steps but switch to a reasoning model (o3-mini) only for the final report synthesis.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're using 03 mini rather than our main model
